title: Tau Earned a Retest: Why Biogen Is Taking Diranersen Into Phase 3 After CELIA Missed Its Primary Endpoint
summary: CELIA missed its prespecified dose-response primary endpoint, yet the lowest dose produced a 0.54-point CDR-SB difference, or 26% slowing, while CSF total tau and tau PET moved in the expected direction. That is enough to justify Phase 3 planning, but not enough to declare tau a validated second disease-modifying pathway.
source_status: Complete professional English adaptation of the approved public Drugnews Facebook/Dcard longform; argument order, clinical figures, investment interpretation, caveats and references retained

card_image_alt: Diranersen lowers tau production and has earned further Phase 3 testing after CELIA

core_judgments: CELIA did not demonstrate that higher or more frequent dosing produced greater benefit, so the prespecified dose-response primary endpoint failed; the 26% secondary signal does not reverse that statistical result.

The 60 mg every-six-months group showed a 0.54-point CDR-SB difference, or 26% slowing, while CSF total tau and tau PET moved in the expected direction. Those aligned signals justify confirmation, not a claim of proven clinical benefit.

The next value inflection point is whether Phase 3 can reproduce cognitive and functional benefit, define a credible dose window, and establish the acceptability of repeated intrathecal dosing and sustained tau lowering.
